cards.title: Operationalizing Uncertainty and Variability in PTA Simulations
cards.claim: Simulations can be based on fixed-effect estimates (typical profile), uncertainty of fixed-effect estimates (probability typical subject meets target), or between-subject variability (range of individual predictions). For PTA, one must distinguish between the probability that a *typical* profile meets a target (driven by parameter uncertainty) and the fraction of a *population* meeting a target (driven by BSV).
conditions: Applicable when constructing PTA curves or CFR estimates.
Requires explicit decision on whether to propagate fixed-effect uncertainty into the PTA calculation or treat fixed effects as point estimates.
required_inputs: Provenance: FDA guidance on simulation types (REF_022).
Input: Fixed-effect parameter estimates and their uncertainty (e.g., standard errors, bootstrap distributions).
Input: Between-subject variability estimates (variance/covariance of random effects).
Gate: Must not assume human IIV from animal data without explicit assumption documentation.
limitations: Human IIV cannot be derived from animal IIV or parameter standard errors without independent human observations.
Residual error must be distinguished from BSV when evaluating observed concentration ranges.
cards.downstream_use: Defines the simulation architecture: whether to sample from fixed-effect uncertainty distributions, random-effect distributions, or both, and how to report the resulting PTA/CFR metrics.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Separate target uncertainty, parameter uncertainty and between-unit variability

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
